root_cause.text: In KVM arm64 nested virtualization, `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0()`/`kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1()` incorrectly used `FIELD_PREP()` on an already `FIELD_GET()`-extracted `xn` value, so the mask for clearing `XN[0]` when `!FEAT_XNX` operated on the wrong bit position and effectively removed the execute-never restriction.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “XN has already been extracted from its bitfield position so using FIELD_PREP() on the mask that clears XN[0] is completely broken, having the effect of unconditionally granting execute permissions,” and the patch fixes `xn &= FIELD_PREP(..., 0b10);` to `xn &= 0b10;` in both execution permission helpers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix XN field masking after extraction so EL0 execute permission is evaluated correctly when XNX is not supported.
intent_record.what: The code changes the mask applied to the local variable `xn` in `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0()` from `FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10)` to the raw value `0b10` inside the `if (!kvm_has_xnx(kvm))` block.
intent_record.how: Because `xn` already holds the extracted field value from `FIELD_GET(...)`, masking it with `FIELD_PREP(...)` uses a shifted bit pattern and can produce incorrect results. Replacing it with `0b10` applies the mask in the field's decoded bit position, so systems without XNX support correctly ignore the unsupported bit and evaluate EL0 execute permission properly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix XN field masking in stage-2 execute-permission decoding by using an unshifted mask on the extracted field value.
intent_record.what: The code changes the mask applied to the local variable `xn` in `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1()` from `FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10)` to the literal value `0b10` inside the `if (!kvm_has_xnx(kvm))` branch.
intent_record.how: Because `xn` already holds the extracted field value from `FIELD_GET(...)`, masking it with `0b10` correctly preserves only the relevant bit in the decoded field representation. This avoids applying a shifted field mask to an already-unshifted value, preventing incorrect execution-permission decoding when XNX is not supported.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct bug: xn has already been extracted with FIELD_GET(), but FIELD_PREP() re-applies the field shift/mask, so the intended clearing/masking of XN[0] for !FEAT_XNX occurs at the wrong bit position and breaks execute-never decoding for EL0.

Same vulnerable pattern in the EL1 helper path: applying FIELD_PREP() to an already FIELD_GET()-extracted xn value misplaces the mask, effectively defeating the intended XN bit handling when XNX is unsupported.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement masks `xn` after `xn` was already extracted with `FIELD_GET()`. Using `FIELD_PREP()` here re-shifts the mask into the original field position instead of applying an unshifted mask to the extracted value, so clearing `XN[0]` when `!FEAT_XNX` targets the wrong bit and can incorrectly remove the execute-never restriction.

Author: Oliver Upton <oupton@kernel.org>

    KVM: arm64: nv: Forward FEAT_XNX permissions to the shadow stage-2
    
    Add support for FEAT_XNX to shadow stage-2 MMUs, being careful to only

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the exact newly introduced logic for FEAT_XNX handling in `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0()` and `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1()`. Both functions do `u8 xn = FIELD_GET(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, trans->desc);`, which means `xn` is already the extracted 2-bit value. They then handle the `!kvm_has_xnx(kvm)` case with `xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);`. This is the vulnerable construct: `FIELD_PREP()` is being applied to an already `FIELD_GET()`-extracted value, so the mask is in the original field bit position instead of the low bits of `xn`. As a result, the intended clearing of `XN[0]` when FEAT_XNX is absent operates on the wrong bit position and does not correctly restrict execute-never semantics. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present (`has_bug=true`), and the correct fix is not present here (`is_fixed=false`).
